decision_description: Resolved the apparent budget-gate contradiction in which the Tier 4 phase7 lump-sum interface-validation artifact (docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json) declared gate_pass_declaration='fail' (no lump-sum response present in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/), while the Tier 4 gate_result.json for gate_09_budget_consistency reported status='pass'. The conflict is between the Tier 4 lump-sum assessment artifact (declaring fail) and the Tier 3 call_binding confirmed instrument type (MSCA-PF), which resolves the budget regime to unit_cost. Applying the C1 instrument-conditional budget gate, the instrument is unit-cost, so the sanctioned budget source is the internal deterministic unit-cost derivation (docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json; total EUR 220723.5; every line item, including the sole host-dependent living-allowance line, resolved to Confirmed), not a lump-sum external response. The lump-sum assessment's 'fail' is not applicable to a unit-cost instrument and cannot block the gate. gate_09 therefore legitimately passed on the four deterministic unit-cost predicates (g08_uc01, g08_uc02, g08_p01, g08_uc03) with the eight lump-sum predicates (g08_p02 through g08_p09) correctly skipped as not applicable for the resolved unit_cost regime, and the pass is inherited into phase8_checkpoint.json with cross-run provenance (original_run_id 49dc10ca-2f91-4922-9f6f-3f9dd6d5a72a).
alternatives_considered: Treat the lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json 'fail' as a blocking gate failure and halt Phase 8 — rejected because the lump-sum interface path does not apply to a unit-cost (MSCA-PF) instrument; applying it would misclassify the instrument and contradict the C1 amendment.
Generate or estimate an internal lump-sum budget to satisfy the lump-sum received/ path — rejected as a §8.3/§13.3-prohibited fabrication/substitution of budget figures.

Silently rely on gate_result.json 'pass' and disregard the coexisting lump-sum 'fail' assessment without logging the resolution — rejected because §12.3 requires the tier contradiction, the prevailing tier, and the reasoning to be recorded explicitly in the decision log.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.1 and §8.4 (C1 instrument-conditional budget gate amendment), applied under the CLAUDE.md §3 authority hierarchy; resolves the conflict between Tier 4 docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/budget_gate_assessment.json (lump-sum path, fail) and Tier 3 docs/tier3_project_instantiation/call_binding instrument type (MSCA-PF, unit-cost regime)
rationale: Under CLAUDE.md §8.1 as amended by C1, unit-cost instruments derive the budget internally by a byte-equal-checked deterministic derivation from published unit costs (confirmed_months x published_rates x host_country_coefficient); this derivation is the exclusive sanctioned budget source for such instruments and is neither fabrication nor a lump-sum estimate. The lump-sum interface validation and its 'fail' result apply only to lump-sum instruments and are therefore not applicable to this MSCA-PF action, so they cannot block gate_09. The instrument type is a Tier 3 confirmed fact and, under the §3 authority hierarchy, governs the budget-regime determination over the Tier 4 lump-sum assessment artifact. The categorical §8.4 Phase-8 block remains fully satisfied because every unit-cost budget component, including the host-dependent living-allowance line, resolved to Confirmed with no unresolved or blocking components. Logging this resolution satisfies §12.3, which requires the resolution method, the tier that prevailed, and the reasoning to be recorded rather than silently resolved by selecting the more convenient source.
